submission.justification: Sensor-T3 has the best unirradiated resolution (about 6 um) but fails the radiation requirement, with 82% efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm^2 against the required 97%. Of the two remaining options, T1 resolves better than T2: about 9 um versus 14-16 um. T1's resolution is nearly flat in thickness, between 8.7 and 9.7 um from 50 to 200 um. The scan points differ by about 0.3-0.5 um, so I can't tell whether the minimum at 125 um (8.75 um) is real or noise. 125 um is therefore a modest optimum, and anything from 125 to 200 um would perform about the same. I did not simulate 250-300 um or T3. I did not simulate T2 above 100 um.

requirements.evidence: Among the radiation-qualified options, T1 gave 8.75 um at 125 um, against 14-16 um for T2. T3 resolves better but is not rad-hard.

requirements.requirement: Technology is one of the three in candidate_specs.md
Suitable for the innermost-layer radiation environment (efficiency >= 97% at 2e16 neq/cm^2)
requirements.evidence: T1 efficiency is 98.5% after 2e16 neq/cm^2. T3 is 82% and fails. T2 is 99.2%.
